official_metrics.Pr_F1eq1_IoU05: per-sample F1 between predicted and GT boxes, success iff F1 = 1; no-target success iff no box; top-1 output caps F1 at 0.67 on 2-target samples
official_metrics.N_acc: over no-target samples, success iff no box predicted
official_metrics.threshold: GREC baselines keep boxes with confidence > 0.7

grefcoco_grec.our_comparability: Our N-acc (gate < .5 on the 8,905 val no-target expressions) matches the official N-acc definition on val, so it is directly comparable as a number (0.5 is our chosen threshold). Official Pr is not comparable: Glance returns one box, so every multi-target sample fails F1 = 1. testA/testB are not evaluated.

citation_mismatches: RC-GRPO: the paper cites only RC-GRPO-II (Qwen3-4B) at 85.3 N-acc, but the same Table 1 lists CRS (Qwen3-4B) at 89.5 val N-acc (above our 87.4) and Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct at 77.2. 'Under a different protocol' overstates the difference for N-acc: the definition (no box on a val no-target expression) matches ours. What differs is Pr and the decision rule.

VenusBench refusal: the paper compares 81.5 with UI-Venus-1.5-8B (61.6), but UI-Venus-1.5-2B (76.3) and -30B-A3B (73.1) in the same Table 9, and Qwen2.5-VL-72B (78.11, VenusBench Table 5), are stronger refusal comparators. v1 still leads all of them, so citing them is both fairer and still favourable.

Same-size comparator omitted: Qwen3-VL-4B appears in VenusBench Table 5 (56.15 overall / 31.55 refusal), Qwen3-VL Table 4 (RefCOCO-avg 89.0, SS-Pro 59.5) and RC-GRPO Table 1 (val N-acc 77.2). The paper uses Qwen3-VL-8B instead.

OpenDecisions sub-scores: the 'Qwen3.5-4B cal' row of the paper's OD table (41.4 / 85.8) is our reproduction; the source's zero-shot base is 46.1 / 81.2 (same capability 63.6). Label the row as our run and add the source row.
VenusBench item count: the source has 6,166 items / 900 refusal (now confirmed); we score 6,165 / 899. Official positive scoring has no ungated option.
Qwen3.5-4B card: RefCOCO(avg) 88.1 and SS-Pro 60.3 have no protocol footnote; ScreenSpot-v2 is not on the card (the paper does not claim it).
